metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

File: /home/hyoklee/cae_test_data/porotomo/dasv_native_PoroTomo_iDAS025_160318160317.h5 (native DAS-HDF5-1.0). The hierarchy is a flat root group `/` containing exactly 8 datasets and 0 nested groups — every node in the file is a dataset.

Complete dataset inventory (path -> shape -> dtype):

| # | Dataset path | Shape | Dtype |
|---|--------------|-------|-------|
| 1 | /channel | (384,) | int32 |
| 2 | /crs | () scalar | uint8 |
| 3 | /das | (30000, 384) | float32 |
| 4 | /t | (30000,) | float64 |
| 5 | /trace | (30000,) | int64 |
| 6 | /x | (384,) | float32 |
| 7 | /y | (384,) | float32 |
| 8 | /z | (384,) | float32 |

Chunking (from the same inspection): /das is chunked with chunk shape (2000, 384); /t and /trace are chunked with chunk shape (30000,); /channel, /crs, /x, /y, /z are contiguous (not chunked).

Attributes (readable ones): /crs carries full CRS metadata — WGS 84 / UTM zone 11N, epsg_code "EPSG:32611" (semi_major_axis 6378137, inverse_flattening 298.257223563, central meridian -117, scale factor 0.9996, false easting 500000, unit metre); /t has units = "seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z". Root-level and several per-dataset attribute listings hit a tool-side bytes-serialization error, so those could not be enumerated (a tooling limitation, not proof of absence).

Consistency note: /das is (samples x channels) = (30000, 384), matching /t and /trace length 30000 and the 384 entries in /channel, /x, /y, /z. Sampling /t gives dt ≈ 0.001 s between consecutive samples -> 1000 Hz sample rate over a ≈ 29.999 s (~30 s) record. The /das data itself was never read whole.

Source: returned evidence from the hdf5 child expert (task_a95963a95508), which opened the file read-only, walked the hierarchy with hdf5_visit/hdf5_list_keys, and queried shape/dtype/chunks/attributes per dataset.
